{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"[section-team supervisor]
You are the SUPERVISOR of section-team. The user talks only to you. You build their projects by doing small work yourself and waking specialist sections for real work. Sections sleep until you wake them.

## Sections (agent type `section-team:<id>`)
Builders: frontend · backend · database · testing · security · devops · uiux · docs · ai-llm · mobile
Advisors (read-only, advise only you): ai-engineer (models, prompts, RAG, agent design) · data-scientist (data, metrics, analytics, ML, experiments)
ai-engineer advises on AI decisions; ai-llm builds AI features.

## When to wake sections
- Small task: about 50 lines of new code or less (one or two small functions): build it and its tests yourself, then run the reviewer gate on your changed files. Give each spec requirement a test that a plausible wrong implementation would fail (NFD instead of NFKD, trim instead of trimEnd, < instead of <=), not only the spec examples. Wake nobody. A feature with its own behaviour to test (a CLI, an endpoint, a module with storage or I/O) is never a small task; input checks that throw do not make a function a feature.
- Single-area task: one kind of work (a CLI, an API, a library, a page, a schema), above that and up to about 600 lines of new code: build the code yourself (and any README it asks for), then wake only the testing section to write and run the tests (give it the files, the behaviour to cover and the spec's edge cases, and ask it to probe every spec line), then run the reviewer gate on your own changed files before you call it done; testing gates its own test files. Wake no builder section. When unsure between this and waking sections for one area, do this.
- Multi-area work: two or more builder areas (for example backend plus frontend, or a database, an API and a UI), or one area clearly bigger than about 600 lines. Wake each needed builder plus the testing section for tests and final verification, and add the docs section when the task asks for docs or a README. Do not build multi-area work yourself, even when the plan is pre-approved. Independent parts run in parallel; parts that touch the same files run one after another.
- An AI or data decision: ask the matching advisor first, then decide. Only you consult advisors.
- 3 or more distinct builders needed (testing, docs and advisors not counted), or a task grows to need a 3rd: first show the user a short plan (which sections, what each does, in what order) and wake nobody until the user says OK.

## How to wake a section
- Agent call: `subagent_type: "section-team:<id>"`. Never pass `model` (sections run on Opus 5.5 from their own files; the Opus reviewer checks the code) and never `name` (not available).
- Keep a list of awake sections and the agent id each spawn returned. Wake each section once per session; a later job for it goes by SendMessage to its agent id, so it keeps its context.
- Every job message contains:
  - the goal; relevant files and decisions so far;
  - `Skills for this job: …` — at most 4, picked from the installed skills and plugins that fit that section and this task (read-only skills for advisors);
  - what "done" means;
  - the agent ids of the awake builder sections, and which of them to coordinate with;
  - "End with your REPORT block."
- Sections message each other directly by agent id and share work through notes. Sections woken in the same message have no ids for each other yet; they use notes, or `main` if they must ask.
- A section falls back to you (`main`) when an id is missing or a message fails: forward its request with SendMessage to the other section's agent id (wake it first if asleep) and include the asker's agent id so the owner replies to it directly. If the answer is a contract, have the owner write or update its note and reply with the note's name.
- A section that reports `Status: blocked` because it needs another section: get what it needs from that section, then resume the blocked one with SendMessage to its agent id.

## Notes
- Sections read `.team/notes/INDEX.md` first, and write a note in `.team/notes/` for anything other sections depend on (an API, a schema, design tokens, a file layout). Shared decisions go in `.team/notes/decisions.md`.
- Point a section to a note ("see the auth note") instead of pasting its content. Do not relay anything that belongs in a note.
- Relay only wake-ups, `Status: blocked` and the fallback above.

## Reports
- Every section ends with a `## REPORT` block. A hook saves it to `.team/reports/<date>/`. If a section ends without one, ask it once with SendMessage for its REPORT.
- A REPORT may name a `Suggested skill:`. List it in your summary and ask the user whether to install it; on yes, install it with the `section-team:add-skill` skill (pass `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` and the skill name) and give it to the section that asked.
- After a task, give the user one summary: one line per section (✅ done / ⚠ partial / ❌ blocked + what it did + its Quality grade), agreements between sections, next steps. Then save the same summary with the Write tool to `.team/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS>-supervisor-summary.md` in the project root (local time; run Bash `date +%Y-%m-%d/%H%M%S` to get it).

## Failures
- A section that fails or stops on an error: resume it once with SendMessage to its agent id. If it fails again, tell the user what failed and the error text.
- A section that ends `Status: partial` on a failing reviewer grade has used its 2 fix rounds: show the user the grade and the open fixes; do not send it back for the same items.

## Your own code
- Before you say work you wrote yourself is done, run Agent `section-team:reviewer` on the changed files (Opus; do not pass `model`). It ends with a GRADE block. Pass: overall at least 8 and no item under 6.
- `section-team:reviewer` replaces `code-reviewer` for your own code.
- Where a spec line can be read two ways, build the stricter reading and say which one you chose.
- Treat every value the spec names as exact (a header value, status code, field, path or format): send exactly that value, never extend it (no `; charset=utf-8` after `application/json`) or normalize it (redirect to the stored URL as given), and add no rule the spec does not state (no extra reserved path, no accepted null).
- If it fails, fix the listed items and review again: at most 2 fix rounds. Then tell the user the grade and what is left.
- A pass ends the gate: do not grade again after a pass.
- Map every OS error your code can hit (a data path that is a directory, a missing parent folder, a file you cannot write, a port in use) by err.code to one friendly line and a non-zero exit (1 unless the spec names a code); detect a missing file by `err.code === 'ENOENT'`, not `existsSync`. Do not create folders or add behaviour the spec does not ask for. A crash path you notice in your own code is a fix before the gate, never a next step.
- Docs-only and config-value edits skip this.

## Rules that win inside section-team
- For delegated work, wake sections. Do not spawn planner, code-reviewer, tdd-guide or other ECC agents yourself for section work; sections use them as their helpers. The one helper type you may spawn yourself is `section-team:reviewer`, for your own code.
- For a multi-section task the testing section owns final review and verification: once the builders have reported, send it the final-review job with each builder's changed files and agent id. Its verdict and any optional findings come back to you in its REPORT; only failing fix lists go to the builders. Do not ask it to send builders a verdict or optional notes. Tell the other sections not to review each other's work; each one still runs its own reviewer gate before it hands back (the plugin refuses an ungraded code REPORT). Never tell a section to skip its gate. After the final review, send a builder only failing items (a spec violation, a crash, a failing grade); list optional findings in your summary as next steps for the user.
- Fable is a consultant sections may use for the hardest problems; the user approves each Fable use.

## New skills
- When the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill, use the `section-team:add-skill` skill.

## Team Board
- Nothing opens by itself. A team strip above the prompt shows the team; `/team` opens the Team Board; `/chats` opens the dashboard of all chats.

## Mode
- This project runs in Balanced mode (default).
- Automatic skill installs: off (from SECTION_TEAM_AUTO_INSTALL_SKILLS).
- A section REPORT with `Status: ungraded` could not run its reviewer gate: run `section-team:reviewer` on its changed files with this mode's gate before you call that work done."}}

commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use only when the user asks for a SessionStart hook committed to their repository. Not for setting up a cloud environment or a repository for cloud sessions; that uses the environment tools. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: section-team:add-skill
commands.description: (section-team) Add a Claude skill from a GitHub URL to section-team. Use when the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill or skill repo and wants it added, or runs /section-team:add-skill <url>. Reviews it for safety, installs it after the user's OK, assigns it to the right section(s) and records that in the team roster.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. # Decisions (supervisor)

- Spec: see `spec.md` (verbatim, final; no human will answer questions; strict reading wins).
- Node built-ins only. Node v22. No npm install.
- File layout:
  - `server.mjs` (backend) — the whole server. Serves the page files by reading them from `public/index.html` and `public/app.js` resolved relative to `server.mjs` (via `import.meta.url`), NOT the cwd. Reads them at request time or at startup — backend's choice, but a missing page file must not break startup checks order (PORT → data file → listen).
  - `public/index.html`, `public/app.js` (frontend).
  - `test/*.test.mjs` (testing): `test/server.test.mjs` (API, spawns `node server.mjs` with PORT=0 and a temp DATA_FILE), `test/page.test.mjs` (static HTML checks + app.js behaviour with a tiny hand-made fake DOM/fetch run via `node:vm`).
  - `package.json`: `{"type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node server.mjs","test":"node --test test/"}}` (testing creates/owns it; backend may create it first).
  - `README.md` (docs).
- Data file layout: `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [ ...booking objects ]}` (backend owns; see backend note when written).

# Full task spec (verbatim from the user — final, no questions possible)

Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install).

Server
- At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order.
- It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `<port>` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout.
- Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`.
- The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file <name>` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening.
- After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders.
- Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before.
- If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.
- Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice.
- Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included.

API
- The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order.
- A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
- Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free.
- A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does.
- `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`.
- `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored.
- `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored.
- `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-e

... [5966 characters truncated] ...

no `<option>` element and none of the room names. When the page loads, the script requests `GET /api/rooms` and fills `#room` with one `<option>` per room, in that order, whose value and text are the room name. If that request gets an error status, `#error` shows the reply's error message and `#room` stays empty; with no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and `#room` stays empty. The first list fetch starts at page load too, without waiting for the rooms reply.
- The list: when the page loads, and each time the Page rules say the list is fetched again, the script requests `GET /api/bookings`, adding `?date=<value>` (the value unchanged) while the value of `#filter-date` is not empty, and replaces the content of `#booking-list` with one `<li>` per booking in the reply's order. Each `<li>` has exactly two child nodes: a text node with exactly the text `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` and no trailing space (for example `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`), then a `<button type="button">` with the text `Cancel`. With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`.
- A list fetch that gets an error status shows the reply's error message in `#error` and leaves the list as it was; one that gets no reply shows `Could not reach the server.` and leaves the list as it was; one that succeeds leaves `#error` alone. When list fetches overlap, only the outcome of the last one started is used: the outcome of every earlier one, an error status or no reply included, changes neither the list nor `#error`.
- Booking: a submit event on the form never reloads the page (the script calls `preventDefault`). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event.

Also add tests with node:test, a `package.json` ("type": "module", a "start" script that runs `node server.mjs`, and a "test" script), and a README with usage.
# Decisions (supervisor)

- Spec: see `spec.md` (verbatim, final; no human will answer questions; strict reading wins).
- Node built-ins only. Node v22. No npm install.
- File layout:
  - `server.mjs` (backend) — the whole server. Serves the page files by reading them from `public/index.html` and `public/app.js` resolved relative to `server.mjs` (via `import.meta.url`), NOT the cwd. Reads them at request time or at startup — backend's choice, but a missing page file must not break startup checks order (PORT → data file → listen).
  - `public/index.html`, `public/app.js` (frontend).
  - `test/*.test.mjs` (testing): `test/server.test.mjs` (API, spawns `node server.mjs` with PORT=0 and a temp DATA_FILE), `test/page.test.mjs` (static HTML checks + app.js behaviour with a tiny hand-made fake DOM/fetch run via `node:vm`).
  - `package.json`: `{"type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node server.mjs","test":"node --test test/"}}` (testing creates/owns it; backend may create it first).
  - `README.md` (docs).
- Data file layout: `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [ ...booking objects ]}` (backend owns; see backend note when written).

# Room bookings

A small meeting-room booking app: one Node.js HTTP server (`server.mjs`) that
serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or later.
- No dependencies: only Node.js built-ins are used, so there is nothing to
  `npm install`.

## Running

```sh
npm start          # same as: node server.mjs
```

Once the server is listening it prints one line to stdout, for example:

```
listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

That is the only thing it ever writes to stdout. The server listens on
`127.0.0.1` only.

Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ in a browser to use the page.

### Environment variables

| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Unset or empty means `3000`. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick a free port; the printed line shows the port actually bound. |
| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the JSON data file. Unset or empty means `bookings.json`. A relative path (the default included) is resolved against the **current working directory**, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |

```sh
PORT=8080 DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
```

### Startup and exit codes

At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts
listening, in that order. It writes one line to stderr and exits with code
`1` when:

- `PORT` is not made only of ASCII digits `0`-`9`, or is above `65535`;
- the port cannot be bound (for example, it is already in use);
- the data file cannot be read for any reason other than "does not exist"
  (for example, the path is a directory), or its content is not in the
  layout the server writes (for example, it is empty or not valid JSON).
  The message is then `cannot read data file <name>`, where `<name>` is
  `DATA_FILE` as given.

A data file that does not exist (or whose folder does not exist) is not an
error: the server starts with no bookings.

## Data file

- Layout: `{"nextId": <integer>, "bookings": [ ...bookings ]}`.
- It is read once, at startup. After that the server's memory is the truth:
  edits made to the file from outside are not noticed.
- It is written only when a `POST` creates a booking or a `DELETE` removes
  one; never at startup or for any other request.
- Every change is saved before its reply is sent, so after a restart with
  the same `DATA_FILE` the bookings and the id the next booking will get
  are as before. Ids are never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
- The server never creates folders. If saving fails (for example, the
  file's folder does not exist), the reply is `500 internal error`, nothing
  changes (the next id included), and the server keeps running.

## Browser page

`GET /` serves the page and `GET /app.js` its script. The page lets you:

- book a room with the form (Room, Title, Date, Start, End, then **Book**);
- see the list of bookings, optionally filtered with **Show date**;
  **Show all** clears the filter;
- cancel a booking with its **Cancel** button.

Error messages from the server are shown on the page as they are; if the
server cannot be reached the page shows `Could not reach the server.`

## API

All JSON replies have `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.
Errors are `{"error": "<message>"}`.

Rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos` (in that order).

A booking looks like this:

```json
{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
```

### `GET /api/rooms`

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/rooms
```

`200`:

```json
{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}
```

### `GET /api/bookings`

Returns every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the room
order above). Add `?date=YYYY-MM-DD` to get only the bookings on that date;
other query parameters are ignored.

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings
curl "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03"
```

`200`:

```json
{"bookings": [
  {"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
]}
```

An invalid `date` (including an empty one, as in `?date` or `?date=`) gets
`400 date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`.

### `POST /api/bookings`

Send a JSON object with `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` (other
keys are ignored) and the header `Content-Type: application/json`.

```sh
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
```

`201` with the new booking:

```json
{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
```

See [Booking rules](#booking-rules) for the error replies.

### `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`

```sh
curl -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1
```

`204` with an empty body. If `<id>` is not a positive integer written in
digits without a leading zero, or no booking has that id:
`404 booking not found`.

### Other replies

| Status | Message              | When |
|--------|----------------------|------|
| `404`  | `not found`          | Any other path, whatever the method (for example `/api/bookings/` or `/api/bookings/1/`). |
| `405`  | `method not allowed` | A known path with a method not listed for it, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` included (for example `GET /api/bookings/abc`). |
| `500`  | `internal error`     | Saving the data file failed, or any other unexpected failure. The server keeps running. |

Paths are matched exactly: no percent-decoding, no dot-segment, slash or
letter-case normalisation (`/API/rooms` and `/api/./rooms` are `404`). The
query string after the first `?` is ignored unless stated above.

## Booking rules

`POST /api/bookings` checks these in order; the first one that fails
decides the reply.

| # | Rule | Status | Message |
|---|------|--------|---------|
| 1 | `Content-Type` media type is `application/json` (case-insensitive, parameters such as `; charset=utf-8` allowed) | `415` | `content type must be application/json` |
| 2 | Body is at most 10000 bytes | `413` | `body too large` |
| 3 | Body is a JSON object (not empty, invalid, `null`, an array or a scalar) | `400` | `body must be a JSON object` |
| 4 | `room` is exactly one of `Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos` (case matters) | `400` | `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
| 5 | `title` is a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming whitespace at both ends | `400` | `title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
| 6 | `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from `2000-01-01` to `2099-12-31` | `400` | `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
| 7 | `start` is `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | `400` | `start must be HH:MM` |
| 8 | `end` is `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | `400` | `end must be HH:MM` |
| 9 | `end` is later than `start` | `400` | `end must be after start` |
| 10 | No overlap with another booking of the same room on the same date | `409` | `room is already booked from <start> to <end>` |

Notes:

- The stored title is the trimmed title. No other field is trimmed or
  changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid.
- Two bookings overlap when each starts before the other ends; a booking
  may start exactly when another ends. The `409` message names the
  overlapping booking that starts earliest.
- Requests sent at the same time are handled as if one at a time: of

Files: `public/index.html`, `public/app.js` (classic script wrapped in an IIFE, `'use strict'`, no globals leaked).

`booking-form` (novalidate), `room` (select, empty in HTML), `title`, `date`, `start`, `end`, `book` (submit),
`filter-date`, `show-all`, `booking-list` (ul), `error` (p, role=alert, empty). One `<h1>`; one `<script src="/app.js">`
as the last element in body. A `<style>` block exists in `<head>` (no inline script, no on* attributes).

## Behaviour (as in spec Page section)
- At setup, in this order, synchronously: `fetch('/api/rooms', {method:'GET'})` then `fetch('/api/bookings', {method:'GET'})`.
  So the first two fetch calls happen during `vm.runInContext`.
- GET requests pass `{ method: 'GET' }` as options. POST passes `{ method, headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body }`;
  DELETE passes `{ method: 'DELETE' }`.
- One `request()` helper: 204 -> body never read (json() not called); any other status -> `await res.json()`;
  fetch rejection or json() rejection -> "no reply".
- Error message: body is non-null non-array object with string `error` -> that, else `Request failed.`
- A 200 list/rooms reply whose `bookings`/`rooms` is not an array shows `Request failed.` (not specified; defensive).
- List: sequence counter; outcome of any non-latest fetch is ignored entirely. Success leaves `#error` alone.
- Rows: `li.append(text, button)` — text is `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>`; empty -> one li with `No bookings.`.
  Uses `list.replaceChildren(...items)`.
- Book: preventDefault first; if `book.disabled` return; disable; POST; `disabled=false` right after the reply+json settle.
- Cancel: guard `if (button.disabled) return;` (a disabled button gets no click in a browser anyway).
  204 -> `#error` emptied; other status -> message; both refetch list. No reply -> message, no refetch.
- Show all: `filter.value = ''` then one list fetch; `change` on filter -> fetch; `input` -> nothing.

- Objects created inside the vm context (e.g. the `headers` object) have the context's Object prototype, so
  `assert.deepStrictEqual(opts.headers, {...})` fails across realms. Compare with `JSON.stringify` or key by key.

I graded `server.mjs` against the spec's Server, API, Booking rules and Page (`GET /`, `GET /app.js`) sections and against `backend-api.md`, line by line. I found no spec violations. I read the whole of `/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/server.mjs` (322 lines) and `package.json`. Bash was denied, so I could not run `node --check` or `git diff`. All the findings below come from reading the code. There are no `test/` files yet, by design.

**Spec checks that pass:**
- **Startup:** the order is PORT, then the data file, then listen (306–318). PORT must be all ASCII digits and at most 65535; an empty or unset PORT means 3000.
- **Data file:** only `ENOENT` means "no bookings"; any other read failure, or content that fails validation, gives `cannot read data file <name as given>` and exit 1. A relative DATA_FILE is resolved against the current working directory.
- **Port in use:** a bind failure is one stderr line with `err.code`, then exit 1.
- **stdout:** only the `listening on …` line is ever written there.
- **Saving:** the file is written only by a POST that creates or a DELETE that removes, and before the reply. If saving fails, the next id and memory stay unchanged (`commit` swaps `store` only after `writeFile` succeeds). The promise queue makes overlapping POSTs give exactly one 201, and one failed save cannot block later requests (`queue = run.catch(...)`).
- **Request bodies:** the body is always read to the end, and at most 10001 bytes are kept, for every route and method.
- **Routing:** paths are compared as raw bytes up to the first `?`. The order of checks is: unknown path gives 404, then a wrong method gives 405. `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/` give 404; `GET /api/bookings/abc` gives 405. A DELETE id must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$`.
- **Booking rules:** rules 1 to 10 are checked in spec order, including 415 before 413, the BOM being kept, ASCII-only lowercasing of the media type, trimming only spaces and tabs, `trim()` on the title, leap years as year % 4, and the earliest-starting conflict for the 409 message.
- **Listing:** `?date` handling uses `has`/`get` as the spec says. Sorting is by date, then start, then room order.
- **Replies:** the JSON content type is exact, and the 204 reply has no body.

**Findings:**
1. **`createApp` is about 100 lines (203–303)**, against the house limit of 50 per function. It is cohesive, but the request handlers live inside it. Moving `listBookings`, `createBooking`, `deleteBooking`, `route` and `servePage` to module level, with a small store/queue object passed in, would fix this.
2. **The save is not atomic (216).** If `writeFile` fails partway (for example disk full or an I/O error after truncation), memory stays correct but the file on disk can be left truncated. The next restart then fails with `cannot read data file`, which breaks the spec's promise that "nothing changes" across a restart. Writing to a temp file in the same folder and then renaming it fixes this without creating any folders.
3. **The catch-all hides the cause of the 500 (298–301).** The user-facing 500 is correct, but the real error is thrown away with no diagnostic. One line to stderr (not stdout) would keep the reply friendly and still not swallow the error.
4. **The 405 ternary is written out four times (268, 273, 278, 281).** A small helper such as `allowOnly(method, expected, handler)` would remove this. It is minor.
5. **`fail` relies on `return undefined` (100–102, 319).** It exits inside the stderr write callback, so `main` has to `return undefined` to keep going cleanly. This is fine, but an explicit `process.exitCode = 1` together with closing would read more clearly. This is optional and costs no points.

content.content: # Team notes — one line per note: — — — spec.md — supervisor — full verbatim task spec (final) — 2026-11-02 decisions.md — supervisor — file layout, data file layout, test command — 2026-11-02 frontend-page.md — frontend — page element ids, fetch call shapes, behaviours, vm-test tips — 2026-11-02 backend-api.md — backend — data file layout + strict load rules, routing/testing gotchas — 2026-11-02 INDEX.md backend-api.md decisions.md frontend-page.md spec.md # Full task spec (verbatim from the user — final, no questions possible) Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. Rejected (stderr `cannot read data file `, exit 1) unless: an object with 10 exactly the keys `nextId` and `bookings`; every booking has exactly the six keys, `id` a positive integer 11 `< nextId`, ids unique, fields valid by booking rules 4-9 (title already trimmed, 1-80), and no two 12 bookings overlap. A UTF-8 BOM makes it invalid JSON -> rejected. `ENOENT` -> empty `{nextId:1,bookings:[]}`; 13 `ENOTDIR` or `EISDIR` etc. -> rejected. 14 - Tests can seed a data file in this layout to start the server with known bookings. 15 16 ## Behaviour worth knowing (tests / frontend) 17 - stdout: only `listening on http://127.0.0.1:\n`. Startup errors: one stderr line, exit 1. 18 Bad PORT line: `invalid PORT: ...`; bind failure: `cannot listen on port

: `. 19 - Every reply body is read in full (buffering stops past 10000 bytes) before replying, for all routes/methods. 20 - Routing compares the raw `req.url` up to the first `?`. Save failure -> 500 `internal error`, memory and nextId 29 unchanged. 30 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` read `public/index.html` / `public/app.js` (relative to server.mjs) on each 31 request; missing file -> 500 `internal error`. 1	# Frontend page (owner: frontend) — 2026-11-02
2	
3	Files: `public/index.html`, `public/app.js` (classic script wrapped in an IIFE, `'use strict'`, no globals leaked).
4	
5	## Element ids
6	`booking-form` (novalidate), `room` (select, empty in HTML), `title`, `date`, `start`, `end`, `book` (submit),
7	`filter-date`, `show-all`, `booking-list` (ul), `error` (p, role=alert, empty). One `<h1>`; one `<script src="/app.js">`
8	as the last element in body. A `<style>` block exists in `<head>` (no inline script, no on* attributes).
9	
10	## Behaviour (as in spec Page section)
11	- At setup, in this order, synchronously: `fetch('/api/rooms', {method:'GET'})` then `fetch('/api/bookings', {method:'GET'})`.
12	  So the first two fetch calls happen during `vm.runInContext`.
13	- GET requests pass `{ method: 'GET' }` as options. POST passes `{ method, headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body }`;
14	  DELETE passes `{ method: 'DELETE' }`.
15	- One `request()` helper: 204 -> body never read (json() not called); any other status -> `await res.json()`;
16	  fetch rejection or json() rejection -> "no reply".
17	- Error message: body is non-null non-array object with string `error` -> that, else `Request failed.`
18	- A 200 list/rooms reply whose `bookings`/`rooms` is not an array shows `Request failed.` (not specified; defensive).
19	- List: sequence counter; outcome of any non-latest fetch is ignored entirely. Success leaves `#error` alone.
20	- Rows: `li.append(text, button)` — text is `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>`; empty -> one li with `No bookings.`.
21	  Uses `list.replaceChildren(...items)`.
22	- Book: preventDefault first; if `book.disabled` return; disable; POST; `disabled=false` right after the reply+json settle.
23	- Cancel: guard `if (button.disabled) return;` (a disabled button gets no click in a browser anyway).
24	  204 -> `#error` emptied; other status -> message; both refetch list. No reply -> message, no refetch.
25	- Show all: `filter.value = ''` then one list fetch; `change` on filter -> fetch; `input` -> nothing.
26	
27	## Testing tips (node:vm fake DOM)
28	- Objects created inside the vm context (e.g. the `headers` object) have the context's Object prototype, so
29	  `assert.deepStrictEqual(opts.headers, {...})` fails across realms. Compare with `JSON.stringify` or key by key.
30	- Text nodes are appended as plain strings: a fake `append` should store strings as text nodes.
31	- Wait a few macrotasks (`setTimeout`) after resolving a fake fetch; json() adds extra microtask hops.

1	# Room bookings
2	
3	A small meeting-room booking app: one Node.js HTTP server (`server.mjs`) that
4	serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.
5	
6	## Requirements
7	
8	- Node.js 22 or later.
9	- No dependencies: only Node.js built-ins are used, so there is nothing to
10	  `npm install`.
11	
12	## Running
13	
14	```sh
15	npm start          # same as: node server.mjs
16	```
17	
18	Once the server is listening it prints one line to stdout, for example:
19	
20	```
21	listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
22	```
23	
24	That is the only thing it ever writes to stdout. The server listens on
25	`127.0.0.1` only.
26	
27	Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ in a browser to use the page.
28	
29	### Environment variables
30	
31	| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
32	|-------------|-----------------|---------|
33	| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Unset or empty means `3000`. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick a free port; the printed line shows the port actually bound. |
34	| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the JSON data file. Unset or empty means `bookings.json`. A relative path (the default included) is resolved against the **current working directory**, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |
35	
36	```sh
37	PORT=8080 DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
38	```
39	
40	### Startup and exit codes
41	
42	At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts
43	listening, in that order. It writes one line to stderr and exits with code
44	`1` when:
45	
46	- `PORT` is not made only of ASCII digits `0`-`9`, or is above `65535`;
47	- the port cannot be bound (for example, it is already in use);
48	- the data file cannot be read for any reason other than "does not exist"
49	  (for example, the path is a directory), or its content is not in the
50	  layout the server writes (for example, it is empty or not valid JSON).
51	  The message is then `cannot read data file <name>`, where `<name>` is
52	  `DATA_FILE` as given.
53	
54	A data file that does not exist (or whose folder does not exist) is not an
55	error: the server starts with no bookings.
56	
57	## Data file
58	
59	- Layout: `{"nextId": <integer>, "bookings": [ ...bookings ]}`.
60	- It is read once, at startup. After that the server's memory is the truth:
61	  edits made to the file from outside are not noticed.
62	- It is written only when a `POST` creates a booking or a `DELETE` removes
63	  one; never at startup or for any other request.
64	- Every change is saved before its reply is sent, so after a restart with
65	  the same `DATA_FILE` the bookings and the id the next booking will get
66	  are as before. Ids are never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
67	- The server never creates folders. If saving fails (for example, the
68	  file's folder does not exist), the reply is `500 internal error`, nothing
69	  changes (the next id included), and the server keeps running.
70	
71	## Browser page
72	
73	`GET /` serves the page and `GET /app.js` its script. The page lets you:
74	
75	- book a room with the form (Room, Title, Date, Start, End, then **Book**);
76	- see the list of bookings, optionally filtered with **Show date**;
77	  **Show all** clears the filter;
78	- cancel a booking with its **Cancel** button.
79	
80	Error messages from the server are shown on the page as they are; if the
81	server cannot be reached the page shows `Could not reach the server.`
82	
83	## API
84	
85	All JSON replies have `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.
86	Errors are `{"error": "<message>"}`.
87	
88	Rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos` (in that order).
89	
90	A booking looks like this:
91	
92	```json
93	{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
94	```
95	
96	### `GET /api/rooms`
97	
98	```sh
99	curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/rooms
100	```
101	
102	`200`:
103	
104	```json
105	{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}
106	```
107	
108	### `GET /api/bookings`
109	
110	Returns every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the room
111	order above). Add `?date=YYYY-MM-DD` to get only the bookings on that date;
112	other query parameters are ignored.
113	
114	```sh
115	curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings
116	curl "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03"
117	```
118	
119	`200`:
120	
121	```json
122	{"bookings": [
123	  {"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
124	]}
125	```
126	
127	An invalid `date` (including an empty one, as in `?date` or `?date=`) gets
128	`400 date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`.
129	
130	### `POST /api/bookings`
131	
132	Send a JSON object with `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` (other
133	keys are ignored) and the header `Content-Type: application/json`.
134	
135	```sh
136	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
137	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
138	  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
139	```
140	
141	`201` with the new booking:
142	
143	```json
144	{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
145	```
146	
147	See [Booking rules](#booking-rules) for the error replies.
148	
149	### `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`
150	
151	```sh
152	curl -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1
153	```
154	
155	`204` with an empty body. If `<id>` is not a positive integer written in
156	digits without a leading zero, or no booking has that id:
157	`404 booking not found`.
158	
159	### Other replies
160	
161	| Status | Message              | When |
162	|--------|----------------------|------|
163	| `404`  | `not found`          | Any other path, whatever the method (for example `/api/bookings/` or `/api/bookings/1/`). |
164	| `405`  | `method not allowed` | A known path with a method not listed for it, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` included (for example `GET /api/bookings/abc`). |
165	| `500`  | `internal error`     | Saving the data file failed, or any other unexpected failure. The server keeps running. |
166	
167	Paths are matched exactly: no percent-decoding, no dot-segment, slash or
168	letter-case normalisation (`/API/rooms` and `/api/./rooms` are `404`). The
169	query string after the first `?` is ignored unless stated above.
170	
171	## Booking rules
172	
173	`POST /api/bookings` checks these in order; the first one that fails
174	decides the reply.
175	
176	| # | Rule | Status | Message |
177	|---|------|--------|---------|
178	| 1 | `Content-Type` media type is `application/json` (case-insensitive, parameters such as `; charset=utf-8` allowed) | `415` | `content type must be application/json` |
179	| 2 | Body is at most 10000 bytes | `413` | `body too large` |
180	| 3 | Body is a JSON object (not empty, invalid, `null`, an array or a scalar) | `400` | `body must be a JSON object` |
181	| 4 | `room` is exactly one of `Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos` (case matters) | `400` | `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
182	| 5 | `title` is a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming whitespace at both ends | `400` | `title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
183	| 6 | `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from `2000-01-01` to `2099-12-31` | `400` | `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
184	| 7 | `start` is `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | `400` | `start must be HH:MM` |
185	| 8 | `end` is `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | `400` | `end must be HH:MM` |
186	| 9 | `end` is later than `start` | `400` | `end must be after start` |
187	| 10 | No overlap with another booking of the same room on the same date | `409` | `room is already booked from <start> to <end>` |
188	
189	Notes:
190	
191	- The stored title is the trimmed title. No other field is trimmed or
192	  changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid.
193	- Two bookings overlap when each starts before the other ends; a booking
194	  may start exactly when another ends. The `409` message names the
195	  overlapping booking that starts earliest.
196	- Requests sent at the same time are handled as if one at a time: of
197	  several overlapping bookings sent at once, exactly one is created and the
198	  others get `409`.
199	
200	## Tests
201	
202	```sh
203	npm test           # runs: node --test test/
204	```
205	
206	The tests use the built-in `node:test` runner and live in `test/`. They
207	start the server with `PORT=0` and a temporary `DATA_FILE`, so they do not
208	touch your `bookings.json`.
209	
210	## Project layout
211	
212	```
213	server.mjs         the server (API, page files, data file)
214	public/index.html  the page
215	public/app.js      the page's script
216	test/              node:test tests
217	package.json       start and test scripts
218	```
219

I read server.mjs and app.js line by line against the spec and found no violations, and every spec line has a test that a likely wrong implementation would fail. Examples are `.trim()` on the Content-Type header (checked with a 0xA0 byte), `<` versus `<=`, choosing the overlap first in the list rather than the one that starts earliest, ids reused after a restart, writing the file on a GET, a missing body drain on 404/405/413/415, stale list fetches, `Book` re-enabled late, and reading the body of a 204. Optional notes, nothing broken: in server.mjs, `readBody` does not settle if the client drops mid-body (it waits on 'end'/'error' only), which costs a little memory but does not affect replies; and on a 500 the server writes a diagnostic line to stderr, which the spec allows.

The booking app is built and its tests pass: I ran `npm test` myself and got 306 passed, 0 failed. I tried to spot-check bad startup settings by hand, but those shell commands weren't allowed here, so that behaviour is checked only by the tests.

| Section | Result | What it did | Review grade |

| backend | ✅ done | `server.mjs` (the whole server) and `package.json` | 8/10 |
| frontend | ✅ done | The page `public/index.html` and its script `public/app.js` | 9/10 |

The testing section's grade was given before a helper added more test cases and tidied up, so those later changes weren't graded again.

**Choices where the spec could be read two ways (I took the stricter reading):**
- **Data file at startup:** the file is stored as `{"nextId": …, "bookings": [...]}`. A file with extra keys, bad or untrimmed fields, repeated ids, ids at or above the next id, or overlapping bookings is refused as `cannot read data file <name>`.
- **Missing file:** only a missing file or folder (`ENOENT`) counts as "no bookings yet". A path that runs through a regular file (`ENOTDIR`) counts as a read failure and exits 1.
- **Odd success replies on the page:** if a 200 reply for rooms or bookings lacks its list, the page shows `Request failed.` and changes nothing.
- **Test command:** it is `node --test test/*.test.mjs`. The planned `node --test test/` fails on Node 22 because it treats `test/` as a file to run.

**Possible improvements (none of them breaks the spec):**
- The server saves by overwriting the data file directly, so a save that fails halfway could leave the file cut short.
- If a client disconnects partway through sending a request body, the server keeps a little memory waiting for it. Replies are not affected.
- In `public/app.js`, the event handlers could catch their own errors, and the reply handling for rooms and bookings is duplicated and could be merged.

The summary is also saved in `.team/reports/2026-11-02/233702-supervisor-summary.md`. Nothing is committed yet.
